items.title: feat(ErdosProblems): Erdős 993 for trees and forests, with spider tie-balance variants
items.body:
## Summary

Adds `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/993.lean`. Closes #1058.

- `erdos_993` (`research open`): the independence sequence of every finite forest (`G.IsAcyclic`) is unimodal. The docstring quotes [erdosproblems.com/993](https://www.erdosproblems.com/993), which asks about "any tree or forest".
- `erdos_993.variants.tree` (`research open`): the tree case. [AMSE87, p. 21](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1987-33.pdf#page=7) treats trees and forests separately.
- `erdos_993.variants.equal_spider_local_tie_balance` (`research solved`): for the equal-arm spider $S(2^k)$ with independence sequence $c_t$, $N_r = \sum_t (t-r)\,c_t\,c_r^t\,c_{r+1}^{k+1-t} \ge 0$ at every rising tie $c_r \le c_{r+1}$ with $r < k$.
- `erdos_993.variants.mixed_spider_one_leaf_local_tie_balance` (`research solved`): the same inequality for $S(2^a, 1)$ at every $r < a$, with no rising-tie hypothesis.

## Proofs

CONTRIBUTING.md asks for long proofs to be hosted externally, so the two `research solved` variants carry `formal_proof` links. They point to the proof development on my fork at [AlperTheKing/formal-conjectures@e9cb4f3c](https://github.com/AlperTheKing/formal-conjectures/blob/e9cb4f3cae9f6f252e553b1874be38e32544b55b/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/993.lean) (branch `erdos993-proofs`, tag `erdos993-proofs-v2`).

- The linked theorems are at L1338–L1343 and L1346–L1350. They use the same definitions and statements as this file.
- That commit builds on Lean v4.27.0 with no warnings.
- `#print axioms` gives only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.

## Context

B. Reynolds' [manuscript](https://github.com/BrettRey/erdos-problem-993/blob/32dbb5d6982147835d4d8f4860e8c2e94efe2f2d/paper/main_v2.tex) (Remark "Tie-fugacity condition") considers two inequalities:

- the tie-fugacity inequality $\mu_T(\lambda_m) \ge m - 1$;
- its mean bound $\mu_T(1) < n/3$, proved for trees on $n \ge 3$ vertices in which every vertex has at most one leaf neighbour.

Together they would give its Conjecture A, $\mathrm{mode} \le \lfloor n/3 \rfloor + 1$. That is a bound on the mode, not unimodality. The manuscript's route to unimodality also needs its Case B hub bound and an injection or Hall argument, and both are open.

The manuscript already proves the leftmost-mode case for $S(2^k)$, and for $S(2^a, 1)$ with $a \ge 3$ (computer-assisted). The variants here hold at every rising tie, or every $r < a$, with closed-form proofs. Spiders are already known to be log-concave, so this gives no new unimodality result. Erdős #993 remains open.

## Checks

`lake --wfail build 'FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«993»'` passes on Lean v4.33.1 (current `main`) with no warnings.

items.title: Add Erdős Problem 543 (random subset sums in abelian groups), link the formal proof
items.body:
Fixes #780.

### What changed
Adds `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/543.lean` with `IsComplete A` (every group element is a subset sum of `A`), `completeProbability G k` (probability that a uniformly random `k`-subset is complete) and `f N` (the least `k` such that this probability is `≥ 1/2` for every abelian group of order `N`):
- `erdos_543` (`research solved`, `answer(False)`): `f(N) ≤ log₂ N + o(log log N)` is false (Ma–Tang / ChatGPT, confirming Erdős' belief). Linked to plby/lean-proofs `Erdos543.not_erdos_543` (Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol; 26 Mathlib-only files).
- Sorry'd literature variants: Erdős–Rényi `f(N) ≤ log₂ N + O(log log N)` and Erdős–Hall's refutation of `log₂ N + o(log log log N)`.

### How checked
- Rebuilt plby's closure against this repo's Mathlib: `#print axioms Erdos543.not_erdos_543` → `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.
- Bridge compiled against the new statement on top of a renamed copy, same axioms (plby phrases "probability ≥ 1/2" as a counting inequality; the bridge shows the two `sInf` definitions of `f` agree since both thresholds are `≤ N`):

<details>
<summary>Bridge</summary>

```lean
open Filter Finset Real

namespace Bridge543

open Erdos543Plby in
lemma halfComplete_iff (G : Type) [AddCommGroup G] [Fintype G] {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card G) :
    1 / 2 ≤ Erdos543.completeProbability G k ↔ Model.HalfComplete G k := by
  classical
  have hfilter : ((univ : Finset G).powersetCard k).filter Erdos543.IsComplete =
      Model.goodSets (univ : Finset G) Model.SubsetSumComplete k := by
    unfold Model.goodSets
    exact Finset.filter_congr fun _ _ => Iff.rfl
  have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < ((univ : Finset G).powersetCard k).card := by
    rw [Finset.card_powersetCard, Finset.card_univ]
    exact_mod_cast Nat.choose_pos hk
  unfold Erdos543.completeProbability Model.HalfComplete Model.totalCount Model.completeCount
  rw [hfilter, le_div_iff₀ hpos]
  constructor
  · intro h
    have : (((univ : Finset G).powersetCard k).card : ℝ) ≤
        2 * (Model.goodSets (univ : Finset G) Model.SubsetSumComplete k).card := by
      linarith
    exact_mod_cast this
  · intro h
    have : (((univ : Finset G).powersetCard k).card : ℝ) ≤
        2 * (Model.goodSets (univ : Finset G) Model.SubsetSumComplete k).card := by
      exact_mod_cast h
    linarith

open Erdos543Plby in
lemma mem_iff {N k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ N) :
    k ∈ {k | ∀ (G : Type) [AddCommGroup G] [Fintype G], Fintype.card G = N →
      1 / 2 ≤ Erdos543.completeProbability G k} ↔ Model.UniversallyHalfComplete N k := by
  simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq, Model.UniversallyHalfComplete]
  refine forall_congr' fun G => ?_
  refine forall_congr' fun _ => ?_
  refine forall_congr' fun _ => ?_
  refine forall_congr' fun hG => ?_
  exact halfComplete_iff G (hG ▸ hk)

open Erdos543Plby in
lemma f_eq (N : ℕ) : Erdos543.f N = Model.universalF N := by
  set S := {k | ∀ (G : Type) [AddCommGroup G] [Fintype G], Fintype.card G = N →
      1 / 2 ≤ Erdos543.completeProbability G k} with hS
  have hN : N ∈ S := (mem_iff le_rfl).2 (Model.universallyHalfComplete_card N)
  have h1 : sInf S ≤ N := Nat.sInf_le hN
  have h2 : Model.universalF N ≤ N := Model.universalF_le_card N
  have hmem1 : sInf S ∈ S := Nat.sInf_mem ⟨N, hN⟩
  have hmem2 : Model.UniversallyHalfComplete N (Model.universalF N) := Model.universalF_spec N
  apply le_antisymm
  · exact Nat.sInf_le ((mem_iff h2).2 hmem2)
  · exact Model.universalF_min ((mem_iff h1).1 hmem1)

theorem erdos_543_bridge : type_of% Erdos543.erdos_543 := by
  show False ↔ _
  simp only [false_iff]
  rintro ⟨o, ho, hf⟩
  apply Erdos543Plby.not_erdos_543
  refine ⟨o, ho.tendsto_div_nhds_zero, ?_⟩
  filter_upwards [hf] with N hN
  rw [← f_eq]
  exact hN

#print axioms Erdos543Plby.not_erdos_543
#print axioms erdos_543_bridge

end Bridge543
```
</details>

items.title: feat(ErdosProblems/1100): add Erdős Problem 1100
items.body:
Closes #1297.

Adds Erdős Problem 1100: let $\tau_\perp(n)$ count the consecutive pairs of divisors of $n$ that are coprime. Is $\tau_\perp(n)/\omega(n)\to\infty$ for almost all $n$? Is $\tau_\perp(n)<\exp((\log n)^{o(1)})$? How does $g(k)=\max\tau_\perp(n)$, over squarefree $n$ with $\omega(n)=k$, grow?

- Definitions: `tauPerp` (with `Nat.nth (· ∣ n)`, as in 1099), `g`.
- Solved: `erdos_1100.parts.i` (yes) and `erdos_1100.parts.ii` (no), by Erdős and Tenenbaum [ErTe89, Corollary 2 and Theorem 4]. Open: `erdos_1100.parts.iii` (`question value`, $`g(k)=\Theta(\text{answer}(k))`$).
- Variants: $\omega(n)\leq\tau_\perp(n)$ (textbook); equality for every $k$ [ErHa78, p. 480]; Erdős and Hall [ErHa78, Theorem 1]; Erdős and Tenenbaum [ErTe89, Theorem 4 and Corollary 2]; the Erdős–Simonovits bounds for $g(k)$ [Er81h, p. 173]; $g(k)\leq 3(3\cdot 2^{-2/3})^k$, the squarefree case of [ErTe89, Theorem 1].
- Notes for reviewers: the page lists the problem as open. As pointed out on the forum (July 2026), [ErTe89] answers the first two questions; I checked Corollary 2 and Theorem 4 in the paper, so parts i and ii are tagged solved. In part ii, $\exp((\log n)^{o(1)})$ is read as: for every $\epsilon>0$, for all large $n$. Part iii reads "determine the growth" as $g(k)=\Theta(\text{answer})$; since even the base of the exponential is open, `(g k)^(1/k) → answer` would also be a reasonable reading, and I can switch to it. The Erdős–Simonovits bounds were announced in [Er81h] without proof; I found no proof of the lower half in print, and [ErTe89, p. 291] calls their argument for squarefree $n$ (the upper half) unpublished. Unrefereed proof claims ($g(k)\gg\varphi^k/\sqrt k$; $`\max_{n\leq x}\tau_\perp(n)=\exp(\Theta(\log x/\log\log x))`$) are not stated.

Checked with `lake --wfail build 'FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«1100»'`.

items.title: fix(ErdosProblems/448): distribution result holds at continuity points
items.body:
`Erdos448.erdos_448.variants.hall_tenenbaum_distribution` required the set `{n | τ⁺(n)/τ(n) ≤ z}` to have a natural density for *every* real `z`. The cited result (Hall–Tenenbaum, *Divisors*, Ch. 4; summarised in Tenenbaum's 2013 survey) is that `τ⁺(n)/τ(n)` has a limiting distribution `ν`: the densities exist and equal `ν(z)` at the continuity points of `ν`. Tenenbaum proves continuity at `z = 1` and lists determining the discontinuity points of `ν`, if any, as an open problem — so the all-`z` statement is strictly stronger than what is known.

**Change**: restate the theorem as `∃ F : ℝ → ℝ, Monotone F ∧ Tendsto F atBot (𝓝 0) ∧ Tendsto F atTop (𝓝 1) ∧ ∀ z, ContinuousAt F z → {…}.HasDensity (F z)` (a distribution function with the density conclusion at its continuity points, as in `ErdosProblems/1002`), update the docstring, and add the Tenenbaum 2013 reference. No other declarations or attributes changed.

**Checked**: `lake --wfail build FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«448»` — Build completed successfully.

**What changed** - `green_32.variants.dirichlet_regime` assumes `101 ≤ ω p` instead of `100 < ω p`. The docstring explains the rounding issue. **Why** `ω` is real-valued, but the set size is `⌊ω p⌋₊` and the required gap is `⌊100 * p / ω p⌋₊`. For `ω p = 100 * p / (p - 1)` and every `c > 0`, eventually `100 < ω p < 101 ≤ c * log p`, so the old hypothesis held, while `⌊ω p⌋₊ = 100` and `⌊100 p / ω p⌋₊ = p - 1`. No dilate of a `100`-element subset of `ZMod p` has a gap of length `p - 1`, so `HasLargeGapDilate ω` fails and the existential statement was false. open Erdos.Problem520

/-- The formal-conjectures random function attached to plby's model. -/
noncomputable def F : ℕ → Omega → ℝ := fun n omega => f omega n

noncomputable instance : MeasureSpace Omega := ⟨μ⟩

  have hmap : Measure.map (fun omega : Omega => omega p) μ = coin := by
    simpa [μ] using Measure.infinitePi_map_eval (fun _ : ℕ => coin) p
  have : μ {omega : Omega | omega p = b} = (Measure.map (fun omega : Omega => omega p) μ) {b} := by
    rw [Measure.map_apply (measurable_pi_apply p) (measurableSet_singleton b)]
    rfl
  rw [this, hmap, coin]
  cases b <;> simp [Measure.dirac_apply' _ (measurableSet_singleton _)]

  measurable_of_prime p hp := by
    have : F p = fun omega => ε omega p := funext (F_prime hp)
    rw [this]; exact measurable_ε p
  iIndepFun_primes := by
    have h := iIndepFun_ε.precomp (g := fun p : Nat.Primes => (p : ℕ)) Subtype.val_injective
    refine h.congr ?_
    intro p
    exact Eventually.of_forall fun omega => (F_prime p.2 omega).symm
  prob_of_prime p hp := by
    constructor
    · have : {omega : Omega | F p omega = 1} = {omega | omega p = true} := by

        simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq, F_prime hp, ε]
        cases h : omega p <;> norm_num
      rw [this]; exact measure_eval_eq p true
    · have : {omega : Omega | F p omega = -1} = {omega | omega p = false} := by
        ext omega
        simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq, F_prime hp, ε]
        cases h : omega p <;> norm_num

  map_mul_of_coprime a b omega h := f_mul_of_coprime omega h
  map_of_not_squarefree n omega h := f_eq_zero_of_not_squarefree omega h

  have hIic : Finset.Iic N = Finset.range (N + 1) := by
    ext m; simp [Nat.lt_succ_iff]
  rw [hIic, Finset.sum_range_succ', partialSum]
  simp [F, f]

    ¬ ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (Ω : Type) [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)]
      (f : ℕ → Ω → ℝ), Erdos520.IsRademacherMultiplicative f →
      ∀ᵐ ω, limsup (fun N ↦ ∑ m ≤ N, f m ω / sqrt (N * log (log N))) atTop = c := by

  have h1 := hall Omega F isRademacherMultiplicative_F
  have h2 : ∀ᵐ omega ∂μ, False := by
    filter_upwards [Erdos.Problem520Plby.normalized_tendsto_zero, h1] with omega hω hlim
    have ht : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => partialSum omega N / Real.sqrt ((N : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log N)))
        atTop (𝓝 0) := by
      rw [tendsto_zero_iff_abs_tendsto_zero]
      refine hω.congr fun N => ?_
      simp only [Function.comp, abs_div, abs_of_nonneg (Real.sqrt_nonneg _)]

      rw [← Finset.sum_div, sum_F]
    rw [hfun, ht.limsup_eq] at hlim
    linarith

  exact h

**What changed** - `Invariant_subspace_problem_finite_dimensional` assumes `[NormedSpace ℂ H]` instead of `[Module ℂ H]`. The docstring explains why. **Why** `[Module ℂ H]` does not relate the complex scalar action to the norm of `H`, so finite-dimensional subspaces need not be closed. Transport the complex structure of `ℂ × ℂ` to the ordinary normed group `ℝ` along a `ℚ`-linear equivalence: this is a complex module of rank `2`, `T = 0` is continuous and linear, but every nonzero complex submodule contains `ℚ x` for some real `x ≠ 0` and is dense, so there is no non-trivial closed invariant subspace. Fixes #6277.

### What changed
Adds `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/1179.lean` with `repCount A g` (`F_A(g)`), `IsBalanced ε A`, `successProbability G ε k` (fraction of `k`-subsets that are `ε`-balanced) and:

Linked to plby/lean-proofs `Erdos1179.erdos_1179` (Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol; three Mathlib-only files).
- `erdos_1179.variants.lower_bound` (also linked): an `ε`-balanced set has `|G| ≤ 2^{|A|}`, i.e. `g_ε(N) ≥ log₂ N`.

Since `g_ε(N)` is defined through an asymptotic probability condition, the upper bound is stated as the existence of an explicit admissible size function rather than through a minimum; the two variants together express `g_ε(N) = (1 + o(1)) log₂ N`.

# Description

> Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that there exists a set $A$ of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$
> in which every $x \in A$ has at least $f(n)$ points in $A$ equidistant from $x$.
> [[Source]](https://www.erdosproblems.com/92)

- Closes the `category test` sanity-check `sorry` on `possible_f_values_BddAbove` introduced in #660 (cc @mo271 ) — the set of feasible values is bounded above, so the `sSup` defining `f` is well-defined.

items.title: ErdosProblems: add 1044, 1047, 1048, 1098, 1121, 1136, 1190, 1193 (#3998 sync)
items.body:
Adds statements for Erdős problems 1044, 1047, 1048, 1098, 1121, 1136, 1190, 1193.

This exhausts the unformalized problems in plby's `sources.yaml` that are not flagged `partial` or `conditional`. Docstrings quote the boxed text on erdosproblems.com verbatim, with the solution sentence copied for solved problems. No `formal_proof` annotations.

Three corrections where the site is wrong, and one bibliography substitution:

- **1047** gives the referee's constant as `5.6^{-6/5}`, where the `.` is a multiplication dot rather than a decimal point: it is $5 \cdot 6^{-6/5}$. For $f(z) = z^6 - z$ we have $f' = 6z^5 - 1$, so at $z^5 = 1/6$ the value is $6^{-1/5} \cdot \tfrac56 = 5 \cdot 6^{-6/5}$. Read as the decimal 5.6 the statement is false.
- **1190** states $\epsilon_m < 1$ without restriction, which fails at $m = 0$: the single congruence $x \equiv 0 \pmod 1$ is admissible, giving $\epsilon_0 = 1$. The variant carries `1 ≤ m`.
- **1044** has "then the the infimum"; corrected.
- **1121** cites `[Ha47]` for Hadwiger's generalisation to convex bodies, but `erdosproblems.com/bibs/Ha47` resolves to Hall, "Cyclic projective planes", Duke Math. J. (1947) — an unrelated paper. The reference list carries the intended Hadwiger, *Nonseparable convex systems*, Amer. Math. Monthly (1947) instead. Reverting to the site's key would mean citing the wrong paper.

Formalization choices:

- **1044**: imports 1041 and reuses its `length` (the 1-dimensional Hausdorff measure) rather than redefining it; both are [EHP58] problems. `IsAdmissible` keeps the product form of the text, with `0 < n` forced by $\prod_{i=1}^n$ — without it $f = 1$ gives an empty sublevel set and the infimum would collapse to 0. "Determine the infimum" uses `IsGLB S answer(sorry)` with the known value 2 in a separate variant.
- **1047**: Pommerenke's $a = (1+\tfrac1k)k^{1/(k+1)}$ is exactly the critical value, so "sufficiently close" is formalized as arbitrarily close rather than throughout a neighbourhood; on one side the two components merge, which would make the neighbourhood reading false. The component count in the referee's example is stated as 6, which the site omits, so that the statement is an instance of the problem's hypothesis rather than a vacuous non-convexity claim.
- **1048**: imports 1043 and reuses its `levelSet`. The box uses the open sublevel set while the text below uses the closed one, and both are followed verbatim: the bullets speak of "the component which contains 0", and at $r = 1$ one can have $|f(0)| = 1$, so 0 would not lie in the open set at all. A nonconstancy hypothesis is added, since $f = 1$ is monic with an empty sublevel set and would falsify the statement for an unrelated reason. `Metric.ediam` is used rather than `EMetric.diam`, which is deprecated in Mathlib v4.27 and would emit a warning that CI treats as a failure.
- **1098**: builds the non-commuting graph as a real `SimpleGraph`, so "complete subgraph" is Mathlib's `IsClique`, and bounds clique size with `Finset.card` rather than `Set.ncard` — the latter is 0 on infinite sets and would make the bound spuriously satisfiable. Carries the batch's one proved declaration, a `simp` lemma unfolding the adjacency by `Iff.rfl`.
- **1121**: circles are closed discs. A line meets the open disc iff it meets the bounding circle, so the separation hypothesis is unchanged, and a convex covering region contains the circle iff it contains the disc, so the conclusion is unchanged. Non-separability is stated as all centres lying strictly on one side, which is equivalent since each disc is connected and misses the line.
- **1136**: reuses `Set.lowerDensity` and `Set.HasDensity`. Müller's set is written in the site's congruence form $3\cdot 2^i \pmod{2^{i+2}}$ rather than the hosted file's odd-part form; the two are equivalent. The upper bound is stated for lower density, following the site, where the hosted file proves the stronger upper-density version.
- **1190**: defines its own `L m = exp(√(log m · log log m))`. Note 202.lean, in the batch 9 PR, defines the same scale as `Erdos202.L`; the namespaces differ so there is no conflict, but they could be unified once both land.
- **1193**: needs no bespoke definitions, reusing `AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep` (which is exactly $1_A \ast 1_A$) and `Set.lowerDensity`/`upperDensity`. The hosted gist states only the counterexample identity and never formalizes either question, so that identity is a variant here.

Part of #3998.

---
Closes #1091
